summary: POC kickoff to scope unit economics for two Hawthorne workloads: interactive customer chat and nightly rerank batch. Discussed success criteria, rough per-token targets, benchmark approach (dedicated nodes + controlled traffic), batching and KV/prefix caching knobs, security gating, and timeline. Agreed to exchange workload samples and run a 2-hour benchmark window next month. Primary concern: staying under $0.00025/token for chat at p95 latency < 250ms; batch rerank budgeted for cost-per-document under $0.005 with throughput target of 200qps during nightly windows.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Mendes (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Hawthorne Head of ML), Priya Singh (Cloud Architect), Rosa Alvarez (Product)
transcript_full:
00:00 Jordan: alright everyone thanks for joining we're on the 15:00 UTC slot for the Hawthorne poc kickoff, I'm Jordan Park, account exec at Redwood. quick goal: align on workloads, success metrics, and a benchmark window. Sofia will do the technical piece.
00:22 Liam: hey thanks Jordan yeah short intros, I'm Liam, I run ML here. Priya handles infra, Rosa for product. we want to understand cost tradeoffs — mainly per-token budget for chat and total run cost for nightly rerank.
00:35 Sofia: great, hi all. I'll sketch a recommended benchmark and the knobs we'll tune — batching, prefix/K V caching, quantization profile. note my speech might have a few typos in the transcript, apologies.
00:48 Rosa: to set context — chat is used in product support with average 4 turns per session, typical prompt length 120 tokens, response around 90 tokens. target: feel snappy. Our finance team gave us a runway constraint so we need per-user cost estimates.
01:10 Priya: infra notes: currently AWS eu-west-1, internal infra is k8s, we can spin up dedicated nodes for the test but networking must stay in our VPC and we need KMS integration. also, we have compliance checklist — SOC2 and SAML.
01:35 Jordan: perfect, on Redwood side we have Hosted, Dedicated, Private options. For this POC we usually run benchmarks with Dedicated pool to get stable numbers and then show equivalence for Hosted. Sofia — quick: rough cost ballpark if we don't tune anything?
01:52 Sofia: un-tuned with a 13B open model quantized to 4-bit on A100-like instance, naive per-token cost for generation is around $0.00035 to $0.0005 depending on throughput. but with continuous batching and KV prefix cache for historical context we can bring that down; target is to get under $0.00025/token for chat at p95 under 250ms. note that's ambitious for interactive.
02:15 Liam: 250ms p95 is pretty tight. our UX team says anything over 300ms feels sluggish. can we do 200ms?
02:23 Sofia: 200ms at p95 with 13B is tough if you have cold KV and no batching. but if most requests hit prefix cache and we keep request windows small, 220-250ms is realistic. Also can trade accuracy: smaller model or quantization to 3-bit could help but might impact quality.
02:42 Priya: on caching — how do you handle KV cache invalidation for chat? We have multi-turn sessions and sometimes context switches.
02:50 Sofia: Redwood supports session-aware KV caching; we can pin session keys and TTLs. For the POC we'll instrument hit-rate metrics. Typical hit rate improvements: 35-60% for repetitive context (like support templates). In transcript that sometimes becomes K V cash or K V cache misheard, just fyi.
03:12 Rosa: on success criteria — here's what product needs: (1) p95 latency < 250ms, (2) per-token average < $0.00025, (3) quality regression < 2% on our eval set (we'll supply test prompts). Are those measurable in your benchmark harness?
03:28 Jordan: yes, measurable. We'll run the benchmark with request tracing and token-level accounting from Redwood Console. Sofia will help map tokens-to-cost in the model catalog.
03:40 Sofia: important: we separate generation tokens vs prompt tokens for cost. We'll report both. Also include warm vs cold starts because KV cache warm-up matters.
03:51 Liam: second workload: nightly rerank. We run a nightly job of ~120k documents, we score them in batches, our tolerance for latency is minutes but cost target is under $0.005 per document on average. throughput needed is ~200 qps during a 10-minute hot window.
04:10 Sofia: rerank is a different optimization surface. There batching wins big — if you can batch 512-1024 items per step we reduce per-doc cost dramatically. For example with a 7B reranker and good batching we can hit $0.0015-0.004 per doc depending on instance. We'll test batch sizes and memory tradeoffs.
04:30 Priya: can we run rerank on lower precision quantized model to save cost? What's the accuracy delta?
04:36 Sofia: yes, quantization and smaller architecture possible. We'll include two model variants in the benchmark: 7B quantized 4-bit and a 13B 4-bit baseline. We'll compute eval metrics against your labeled set to measure regression.
04:54 Rosa: timeline ask — finance wants a go/no-go decision in 3 weeks. Can we produce benchmark numbers and a clear cost playbook in that window?
05:03 Jordan: yes — plan: week 1 collect datasets and SLOs, week 2 run bench, week 3 analyze and present. target deliverable: cost-per-token table, recommended batching/cache params, and an ops playbook.
05:18 Priya: networking and security gating: we need KMS, SAML SSO, audit logs. Is that available for POC or only for private deployment?
05:27 Sofia: we can integrate KMS and SAML for Dedicated test beds; audit logs available in Console with retention controls. For the POC we can use Redwood Dedicated inside your VPC via our Private deployment conduit (note: might require a short infra onboarding). I'll send the security brief with required artifacts.
05:45 Liam: any gotchas around token accounting accuracy? We want end-to-end numbers inclusive of tokenization differences.
05:52 Sofia: we instrument at request boundary and also at output tokens after our tokenizer step. We'll align tokenizers with your preprocessing to avoid mismatch. small transcription glitch: tokenizer sometimes called "tok-nizer" in notes.
06:10 Jordan: competitors were mentioned — Liam, do you have any constraints from previous evaluations vs Anthropic or Google Vertex?
06:16 Liam: we've run initial evals vs Vertex and results comparable but cost with Vertex was higher in our early tests. Also our infra team prefers a model runtime that supports flexible on-prem later. That's why Redwood's Dedicated and Private were interesting.
06:33 Sofia: okay back to benchmarks — approach: we do two benchmark modes for each workload: (A) controlled dedicated window with stable load to measure unit economics and SLOs, (B) hosted-like bursty pattern to see tail behavior and fallback. We'll run multiple seeds to account for variance.
06:51 Rosa: for chat workload what's the sample RPS we should provide? We can simulate 10 rps steady and then peaks to 35 rps for flash support events.
07:00 Sofia: that works. We'll need distribution of prompt/response lengths and multi-turn distributions — ideally a CSV with session lengths and token counts.
07:10 Priya: about cost per token: can you share a sample formula? I'd like to show finance a spreadsheet before the bench.
07:16 Jordan: I'll share a live spreadsheet but quick sample: raw inference cost + infra delta + orchestration overhead divided by output tokens. Example cell: instance-hour cost * fraction used / tokens generated. Sofia will populate numbers for A100-like and V100-equivalents.
07:35 Sofia: practical knobs: batch size (in-flight tokens), max latency cap per request (we can drop batching beyond X ms), KV cache TTL and session pinning ratio, and model quantization profile. We'll sweep batch sizes of 1, 4, 8, 16 for chat and 64-1024 for rerank.
07:58 Liam: on the chat side, how do you prevent batching from increasing tail latency?
08:04 Sofia: Redwood runtime uses adaptive batching with per-model latency SLOs; we can cap batch wait time and fallback to single-call for sub-100ms. We'll show p50/p95/p99. There will be tradeoffs: more batching reduces cost but increases p99 unless KV cache offsets generation time.
08:25 Rosa: QA note — we will provide an eval set for quality regression checks. What thresholds do you normally recommend? We suggested < 2% BLEU loss ? Not sure BLEU is right.
08:36 Sofia: we'll use your task-specific metrics; for chat it's best to use a holdout of human-labeled preferability or classification accuracy. We'll run automatic metrics but keep human-in-the-loop for final decision.
08:50 Jordan: security doc delivery: Sofia will send the SOC2 brief and link to the compliance packet. Also will include IP egress controls for VPC.
09:03 Priya: do you have recommended instance families? We're on AWS.
09:07 Sofia: for the POC we recommend p4d-like for 13B and g5 or cheaper for 7B. We'll include lower-cost families to show sensitivity. Also will include an edge-case run for quantized lower-memory instances.
09:25 Liam: what's the expected variance in measured per-token cost between runs?
09:30 Sofia: usually 5-15% variance if warm cache and stable load. Cold starts and noisy neighbors add more. That's why dedicated run preferred to show deterministic numbers.
09:45 Jordan: ok let's talk deliverables — the spreadsheet will include: per-token cost table, per-request cost, recommended batch/cache parameters, estimated monthly run-rate for your projected traffic, and risk notes. Does that cover it?
09:58 Rosa: yes. Also include a simple ops playbook for fallbacks and canary rollout notes.
10:06 Sofia: we'll include recommended canary policy: start 10% traffic on smaller quantized model, monitor latency and quality, then ramp. Also note automatic fallback to hosted baseline if Dedicated nodes overloaded.
10:24 Priya: about data — we want to keep PII inside our VPC. Will Redwood process data inside our VPC for Dedicated POC?
10:31 Sofia: yes, Dedicated in VPC keeps inference inside. We'll provide instructions for network allowlists. For Private on-prem we can take an air-gapped install later.
10:45 Liam: any rough ballpark numbers you can drop now for finance?
10:49 Jordan: quick summary for discussion — chat baseline un-tuned $0.0004/token, tuned with caching and batching $0.00018-$0.00025/token. Rerank per doc $0.0015-$0.005 depending on batching and model size. We'll validate these in the bench.
11:12 Rosa: great. If we hit $0.00022/token with p95<250ms and quality within 2% we greenlight a 3-month pilot.
11:23 Jordan: perfect. final recap of next steps: Jordan share spreadsheet and benchmark harness link, Hawthorne to provide workloads and SLOs, Sofia to share security docs, schedule benchmark window. We'll reconvene after bench analysis.
11:40 Priya: I will upload logs and dataset by 2026-03-04.
11:45 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll send calendar invites for the benchmark window and follow ups.
11:52 Meeting ends.
